newsitem.title: PERU: Red Cross provides for Peru hostages' needs.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross provides for Peru hostages' needs.

text.p: In the 31 days since Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) gunmen stormed a cocktail party at the Japanese ambassador's residence, the Red Cross has delivered everything from food and water to chess sets and guitars, the organisation said on Friday.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has tried to provide everything hostages held by Marxist rebels in Peru might need to ease their ordeal during the month-long siege.
In food alone, the Geneva-based Red Cross has taken 7,402 meals into the besieged diplomatic mansion, including 1,531 Japanese-style dishes to suit the palates of the dozens of captives from Japan.
Hostages have been given 997 articles of clean clothing to replace the elegant outfits they wore to the reception, and toothbrushes, razors, soap and shaving cream to keep up appearances.
Cigarettes, books, playing cards and board games have been ferried into the residence to help pass the long hours of captivity, the ICRC added.

Released hostages have praised the work of Red Cross workers, in particular the regular deliveries of messages from family members. A total of 2,641 letters have been exchanged between hostages and relatives since the crisis began, the Red Cross said.

The rebels held 73 hostages on Friday, down from more than 500 at the time the residence was seized, including top government and security force officials, dozens of Japanese businessmen and diplomats and the younger brother of Peru's President, Alberto Fujimori.
